title: Infiniband dissector: Implement FLUSH and ATOMIC Write dissector
description:
FLUSH and ATOMIC Write were newly added in IBTA Specification v1.5. The SoftRoCE driver (linux kernel) has already enabled the operations[1][2], and there is already an example application that uses these operations[3]. IB SPEC: https://cw.infinibandta.org/site/login

This patch series enables to analyze packets of these new operations. I made the patches referring to IBTA Specification v1.6. Please note that **the spec is proprietary and MEMBERS ONLY**, and **it is not allowed to quote any part of them on this thread**. While I believe my work is complete, please tell me the corresponding section or the page number if you find any error. Sorry for inconvenience, but it cannot be helped.


I got a packet capture of these operations. To help reviewers, I attach a part of the output below.

- Patch 1:
The first patch simply defines the new operations according to the spec.
After applying the patch, packets can be detected by tshark like this:
```
    9   0.004996 192.168.10.10 → 192.168.10.11 RRoCE 78 RC Flush QP=0x000017
   10   0.005004 192.168.10.10 → 192.168.10.11 RRoCE 82 RC Atomic Write QP=0x000017
```

- Patch 2:
The second patch makes it possible to parse FLUSH packets.
Here is an example output from 'tshark -V -r <filename>' command. 
```
InfiniBand
    Base Transport Header
        Opcode: Reliable Connection (RC) - FLUSH (28)
        0... .... = Solicited Event: False
        .0.. .... = MigReq: False
        ..00 .... = Pad Count: 0
        .... 0000 = Header Version: 0
        Partition Key: 65535
        Reserved: 00
        Destination Queue Pair: 0x000017
        1... .... = Acknowledge Request: True
        .000 0000 = Reserved (7 bits): 0
        Packet Sequence Number: 7619090
    FETH - FLUSH Extended Transport Header
        0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 000. .... = Reserved (27bits): 0
        ...0 0... = Selectivity Level: 0
        .... .010 = Placement Type: 2
    RETH - RDMA Extended Transport Header
        Virtual Address: 0x00007f54cc600010
        Remote Key: 0x00001462
        DMA Length: 17 (0x00000011)
    Invariant CRC: 0x1676363c
```
parse_FETH() was added to parse 'FLUSH Extended Transport Header'.

- Patch 3:
The third patch makes it possible to parse ATOMIC Write packets.
Here is an example output from 'tshark -V -r <filename>' command. 
```
InfiniBand
    Base Transport Header
        Opcode: Reliable Connection (RC) - ATOMIC WRITE (29)
        0... .... = Solicited Event: False
        .0.. .... = MigReq: False
        ..00 .... = Pad Count: 0
        .... 0000 = Header Version: 0
        Partition Key: 65535
        Reserved: 00
        Destination Queue Pair: 0x000017
        1... .... = Acknowledge Request: True
        .000 0000 = Reserved (7 bits): 0
        Packet Sequence Number: 7619091
    RETH - RDMA Extended Transport Header
        Virtual Address: 0x00007f54cc600008
        Remote Key: 0x00001462
        DMA Length: 8 (0x00000008)
    Invariant CRC: 0xd8b788c1
Data (8 bytes)

0000  21 00 00 00 00 00 00 00                           !.......
    Data: 2100000000000000
    [Length: 8]
```
Unlike FLUSH, new parser is not necessary.

- Patch 4:
This is a trivial fix of comment.


[1] [PATCH v7 0/8] RDMA/rxe: Add atomic write operation
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-rdma/1669905432-14-1-git-send-email-yangx.jy@fujitsu.com/

[2] [for-next PATCH 00/10] RDMA/rxe: Add RDMA FLUSH operation
https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20221206130201.30986-1-lizhijian@fujitsu.com/

[3] Example of performing an RPMA atomic write to a persistent memory region
https://github.com/pmem/rpma/tree/main/examples/07-atomic-write

commits_data.title: Infiniband dissector: Add definitions of FLUSH and ATOMIC Write
commits_data.message:
Infiniband dissector: Add definitions of FLUSH and ATOMIC Write

FLUSH and ATOMIC Write were newly added in IBTA Specification 1.5. This
patch adds the definitions of these new operations. Wireshark can now
distinguish the packets just like this:
  RRoCE 78 RC Flush QP=0x000017
  RRoCE 82 RC Atomic Write QP=0x000017

Signed-off-by: Daisuke Matsuda <matsuda-daisuke@fujitsu.com>
